summary:
Designing a space mission involves far more than launching a spacecraft. Every decision, from choosing an orbit to selecting scientific instruments, comes with trade-offs that determine whether a mission succeeds.

We developed Mission Architect, an interactive simulator that allows users to experience these challenges firsthand. Participants can design spacecraft, select components and launch vehicles, and work within constraints of budget, mass, power, and communication. Through simulation, they can explore how their decisions affect mission feasibility and scientific outcomes.

Our aim was to make aerospace engineering accessible to students beyond textbooks, giving them the freedom to experiment, make mistakes, and understand real engineering challenges.

However, given the limited development time, we couldn't model every aspect with the scientific accuracy we had envisioned. Some simulations remain simplified, and we hope to improve their realism in future versions.

Mission Architect is our attempt to make learning science an experience rather than just an explanation.
details: Project Details: Mission Architect Designing a space mission is a fascinating challenge because every engineering decision affects several others. We developed Mission Architect, an interactive space mission simulator that allows users to experience this process firsthand, from designing a spacecraft to evaluating the feasibility of a mission. Users can select mission objectives, choose spacecraft components, scientific instruments, launch vehicles, and orbital parameters, while managing constraints such as budget, mass, power, and communication. The simulator helps them understand how these decisions influence mission performance and scientific outcomes. Our primary aim was to make aerospace engineering more accessible and engaging, particularly for students. Instead of simply reading about spacecraft and orbital mechanics, users can experiment with their own designs, encounter engineering challenges, and learn through trial and error. We hope this encourages curiosity, computational thinking, and an appreciation for the complexity of space exploration. For development, we worked with React, TypeScript, and Three.js, using web technologies to create an interactive interface and three-dimensional visualizations. What makes our project creative is its attempt to bring together several aspects of space mission planning into a single learning experience. Rather than focusing on just one concept, we wanted users to understand how different engineering systems interact and why even seemingly small decisions matter. Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, user experience, computational performance, and the limited time available to us. Although we couldn't make every simulation as scientifically accurate as we had initially envisioned, we focused on communicating the fundamental engineering principles while keeping the experience engaging. Ultimately, Mission Architect reflects our belief that science becomes far more exciting when we get to explore the problems scientists and engineers actually solve.
